narrative:
The model determined that you have a 40% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability is high enough to cross the bank's approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, your installment rate as a percentage of disposable income, and the level of savings you currently hold. Your checking account being in negative balance (<0 DM) was the single biggest reason for the denial. Among approved applicants, only 12.6% have a negative account status, while 59% have no checking account at all. This negative status pushed the prediction strongly toward bad credit risk.

Your requested installment rate of 2% of disposable income actually worked in your favor. It is lower than the 3% average seen among approved loans, which helped pull the prediction back toward approval. However, this positive effect was not large enough to overcome the other signals.

Your low savings balance (under 100 DM) also increased the perceived risk. Nearly half of all applicants fall into this same low-savings category, but combined with the negative checking account it added further weight toward denial.

The model did not consider your age, gender, or foreign-worker status in any way.

To improve your chances on a future application, focus first on bringing your checking account balance above zero and building at least a modest savings cushion. Even modest improvements in these two areas can meaningfully change how lenders view your application. Consider reapplying once those balances have stabilized.
